newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-A mug's guide to rugby.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-A mug's guide to rugby.

text.p: WELLINGTON, July 24 - Melburnians have been bombarded with footy stories all week -- in their newspapers, on television, on the radio.
Nothing unusual about that in Melbourne, except this footy is a different shape and size to the Aussie Rules one they're used to.
It's used in this game called rugby union, which has attracted nearly 100,000 to the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday, despite most of Melbourne having no idea what the game involves.
A Melbourne newspaper this week tried to help its readers with a two-page spread of a "mug's guide" to rugby.
Remember these three simple laws -- a player cannot pass the ball forward, you don't laugh when New Zealand does the haka, and the All Blacks invariably win.

This is not rugby league. This is something more aesthetic, more operatic, more hands-on, more international. This is a barbaric sport played by gentlemen, unlike rugby league, which is a barbaric sport played by barbarians.
On scrums: Sixteen forwards bashing their heads into each other is somewhat uncouth, but it does mean something. It is the crux of the matter. Just nod accordingly.
On lineouts: One of the most spectacular parts of the game, even if it makes little sense.
On rucks: A player when tackled has to release the ball near him on the ground, which prompts each team's forwards to jump all over him.

On player positions: The acrobats are the two second-rowers. The midget is the halfback, who tosses the ball into the scrum. He dives a lot. He does that because it looks good. The wingers are the show-ponies.
John Eales: He is the best. Eales is a phenomenon. He is easily among the top five rugby players this country has produced. He is up there with David Campese and Mark Ella.
Tim Horan: It has taken some time for Horan to settle into this difficult spot (first five-eighth). He will get there because he is too good a player not to.
Sean Fitzpatrick: Without doubt, he has been the greatest international hooker of the past 20 years. The best sledger on the world circuit. He is the Shane Warne of rugby.
Christian Cullen: Vies with Matt Burke as the world's best fullback. Cullen is the master of creating "turning points".
